llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed document-generation and optional form-assistance workflow for software copyright registration, with review needed for generated legal/application wording.

dimensions.detail: The scripts read a user-specified repository or directory, generate DOCX/Markdown registration materials, and optionally assist with browser-based form filling; these capabilities fit the stated software copyright registration purpose. The generated fallback function and technical descriptions can be generic, so users must verify them before use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow discloses GitHub URL or local-path input, temporary cloning, local source/README analysis, output file creation, user confirmation before online filling, and a prohibition on automatic submission. It does not provide formal permission metadata, but the operational scope is visible in the skill instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Artifacts consist of SKILL.md and three Python helper scripts with no install hooks, background setup, dependency-install commands, or obfuscated behavior. Static scan reported no findings and VirusTotal telemetry was absent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local file reads, output writes, optional GitHub cloning, and headed-browser use are proportionate to generating registration materials and assisting with a government web form, provided they remain limited to the user-selected repo, output directory, and explicit browser session.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, credential-store access, background workers, destructive actions, or automatic submission are present. Login is user-performed and final submission is explicitly blocked pending user control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Use this only on repositories you are comfortable having read and summarized. Before filing anything, carefully review the generated function and technical-description text, because parts may be generic placeholders rather than verified facts. Keep the output directory explicit, approve any GitHub clone and browser session yourself, and do not allow final submission of an official application without manual review.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill necessarily reads selected source files and writes generated documents. The lack of formal permission declarations is a transparency weakness, but the artifact instructions disclose the source path, output files, and review step.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The fallback main-function text can make unsupported capability claims. This is a document-accuracy risk for official filing materials, but the workflow presents generated content for user review and does not automatically submit it.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The fallback technical-features text can assert architecture and deployment properties without strong evidence. This should be treated as draft language requiring manual verification, not as malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Cloning a user-provided GitHub URL and writing generated files are expected for this workflow. Users should still confirm the repository URL, destination, and output path before running it.
